problem: SDK memoized start and close exposed Python owner Tasks. A direct cancelled waiter could stop the shared handshake or leave a child midway through the shutdown/EOF/termination ladder.
implementation: Owner-held SharedPromise for initialization and CleanupPromise for process close preserve synchronous entry, stable identity, independent observers, original failure/cleanup/retry rules and complete stream/process reaping.

paired.scope: Actual pinned scripted Node runtime driven through original and Python SDKs. Handshake abandonment/timeout, failed initialization with original ordered cleanup and one retry, close abandonment/timeout, one handshake per successful instance, final exit/pipe/pending-request checks.

existing_pair.scope: Existing actual wire/subagent success, malformed/protocol/transport and error-folding observations unchanged

native.scope: Actual Python wire peer for cancellation/timeout/reaping, SDK run, provider activation/unload, stdio cold resume/wait and transport consumers

source.scope: Original sdk-client, dispose and run suites

baseline: Controlled pre-fix close owner became cancelled when its direct observer was cancelled; no process created for the baseline reproduction.

cleanup.removed: Owned synthetic peer/workspace/home/tmp and paired runtime marker files after final consumer
cleanup.retained: Commands, raw Source/native observations, precise SDK Source hashes, XML/logs and baseline; shared Source/toolchains remain needed until C9

limitations: Modern Node is used only in the fixed Source comparison environment. Production SDK launches the Python/Win7 runtime.
This is targeted ownership verification, not coordinated pin promotion or release qualification.
